question.text: Mr. Vikram Bhatia is a Lead Investor raising a Syndicate of INR 40 crore for a Pre-Series A in 'Zephyr Robotics'. He commits INR 8 crore himself and raises INR 32 crore from co-investors at a 20% carry. Exit at INR 120 crore after 3 years. How much carry does Mr. Vikram receive from the syndicate co-investors' profits? (Chapter 9 carry convention: carry is on profit, not gross.)

answer.text: INR 24 crore — 20% of the gross exit proceeds.
INR 16 crore — 20% of the total investment-exit delta (120 − 40) = 80 crore.
INR 16 crore × 80% = INR 12.8 crore — carry only on the co-investors' portion of profit, since Vikram himself cannot earn carry on his own capital contribution.
INR 8 crore — carry equals his own committed capital.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Total exit = 120 cr; Total investment = 40 cr; Profit = 80 cr. Vikram's own contribution is 8/40 = 20% of syndicate, co-investors' share = 80% = 32/40. Co-investors' profit share = 80 × 0.8 = 64 cr. Carry = 20% × 64 = INR 12.8 cr. Vikram does not earn carry on his own committed capital (no self-dealing). This is the Chapter 9 example mechanic with different numbers. **The Trap:** Option A ignores invested cost (carry is on profit not gross). Option B includes Vikram's own contribution in the carry base. Option D has no formulaic basis. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tested syndicate carry. XIX-A tests it at distributor level (as a product feature). XV tests carry structures in PE research valuation. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Document in the Syndicate LLP agreement that carry is measured only against non-lead contributions. Also specify the hurdle (commonly 8%) and whether catch-up applies. Lead investors who fudge this line get sued at exit — SEBI's Accredited Investor Framework requires clear disclosure.
